summary: Pier Gabriele Goidanich was a linguist who studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore and the University of Milan under Graziadio Isaia Ascoli. He served as professor at the University of Pisa and the University of Bologna.

Piero Martinetti was a philosopher and Indologist who studied under Giovanni Flechia at the University of Turin and at the University of Leipzig. He held professorships at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano and the universities of Milan and Turin.
Pierre Arènes is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under André Bareau. He held a post at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (attested 2003–2004).

Pierre Bourdieu was a scholar in philosophy and other fields who studied under Émile Benveniste and at the École Normale Supérieure. He held posts at Lille University, the Faculty of Arts of Paris, EHESS, and the Collège de France.

Pierre Chantraine was a linguist who studied under Alfred Ernout, Antoine Meillet, Joseph Vendryes, and Theodor Bloch. He served as directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and professor at the Sorbonne and University of Paris.
Pierre Charles Olloba d'Ochoa was an Indologist who studied under Garcin de Tassy at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales in 1839.

Pierre Dupont was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. Educated at the École du Louvre, EPHE, and Institut d'ethnologie under scholars including Sylvain Lévi and Alfred Foucher, he held posts at the EFEO, EPHE, and Sorbonne.

Pierre Fabricius was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Heidelberg, Hamburg, and SOAS under Heinrich Zimmer, Walther Schubring, Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Louis Renou. He served as professor at the Royal University of Phnom Penh.

Pierre Fallon worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at KU Leuven and the University of Calcutta. He taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and served as professor of French literature at the University of Calcutta.

Pierre Herman Leonard Eggermont was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He studied at Leiden University under Frederik David Kan Bosch, with additional study under Louis Renou and others. He held academic posts at the University of Amsterdam and KU Leuven.

Pierre Johanns was an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar educated at KU Leuven and Oxford. He taught philosophy at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and St. Mary's College, Kurseong, and taught Sanskrit at the University of Namur.

Pierre Meile was an Indologist and linguist who studied at ENS and Visva-Bharati under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, Antoine Meillet, Émile Benveniste, and others. He held a professorship at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales.

Pierre Rolland was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Paris, Aix-Marseille, Göttingen, Tübingen, and Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann, Louis Renou, and Armand Minard. In 1969, he became a researcher at the National Centre for Scientific Research.

Pierre-Amédée Jaubert was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistic scholar who studied under Silvestre de Sacy. He served as professor at the Collège de France, director at INALCO, and president of the Société Asiatique.
Pierre-Gustave Garrez was an Indologist who completed his studies at Lycée Henri-IV and Lycée Louis-le-Grand.

Pierre-Philippe Giraudeau was a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the Séminaire des Missions Étrangères de Paris and became a missionary for the Paris Foreign Missions Society in 1877.

Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Louis Renou. He held posts at the French Institute of Pondicherry, EFEO, EHESS, and served as Chair of Sanskrit at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and linguist. He completed his Ph.D. at Leiden University, where he also served as a research fellow (attested 1996).

Pieter Hendrik Pott was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and archaeologist who studied under Frederik David Kan Bosch at Leiden and Utrecht. He held curatorial posts at the National Museum of Ethnology and served as professor of museology at Leiden University.
Pieter Jacob Cosijn was a linguist who studied at Utrecht University from circa 1860 to 1867. He later held a post at Leiden University from 1877 to 1899.
